confirmed: Code plugins can declare a validated spider.runtime contribution only with the explicit spider.runtime permission; the API prefix and operation names are validated against an allowlist.

PluginHost exposes only installed, enabled, permissioned contributors. The main-process provider adapts those contributors into SpiderFactory and checks current plugin state for each operation, so cached Spider instances stop dispatching after disable or uninstall and can use a replacement plugin generation.

The host-initiated invoke/reply/cancel protocol bounds JSON payloads, limits in-flight calls, caps timeouts, and cancels pending work on caller abort, timeout, worker failure, disposal, disable, replace, and uninstall.
The fixture plugin runs locally in tests; no third-party runtime code was fetched from the network.

trustBoundary.currentImplementation: Third-party plugin code uses the existing Worker thread plus node:vm execution model.
trustBoundary.consentModel: The spider.runtime permission is explicit in the manifest/permission flow. The install confirmation warns that Worker/node:vm is not a security boundary and says to install code only from trusted sources.
trustBoundary.limitation: Worker threads and node:vm do not isolate arbitrary untrusted code. The implemented choice is trusted-code consent, not OS-process isolation. Plugins must be treated as trusted executable code; this work does not claim protection from malicious code or synchronous infinite loops.
trustBoundary.requiredFollowUp: If arbitrary or untrusted plugins must be supported, move execution to an OS subprocess with an enforced sandbox and a narrow RPC protocol before advertising that security property.

changes: Added Spider runtime contribution schema and strict manifest validation, including explicit permission and operation allowlist.
Added provider composition into SpiderFactory through PluginHost, with active-generation lookup and JSON-only request/reply/cancel handling.
Added bounded, cancellable host-initiated RPC and deterministic worker/request disposal on plugin lifecycle changes.
Added a local fixture plugin and tests covering installation, SpiderFactory dispatch, operation failure, abort, timeout, payload bounds, replacement, disable, uninstall, and provider retirement.
Committed implementation and fixture separately from evidence as GitButler commit lrn on codex/architecture-cleanup-20261025.
